title: Houthis Claim Saudi Forces Targeted Yacht Carrying 14 Indians in Red Sea
excerpt: A Houthi spokesman said Saudi forces struck an Indian yacht near Zuqar Island and that Yemeni forces rescued the 14 Indian nationals aboard. The claim has not been independently verified, and came a day after attacks in Saudi Arabia killed and injured Indian workers.
body:
• Yemen's Houthi movement claimed on Thursday that Saudi forces targeted a yacht carrying 14 Indian nationals near Zuqar Island in the southern Red Sea.
  • Houthi spokesman Yahya Saree said Yemeni armed forces rescued the 14 Indians and would release further details. The claim had not been independently verified at the time of reporting, and Saudi Arabia had not commented in the reports.
  • The claim follows the October 21 attacks on King Fahd International Airport in Dammam and Aramco's Shaybah oil field, in which Indian nationals were killed and injured.
  • India's Ministry of External Affairs has condemned the attacks on civilian and energy infrastructure in Saudi Arabia and called for an immediate halt to strikes on such targets.

Yemen's Houthi rebels claimed on Thursday that Saudi Arabia targeted a boat carrying 14 Indian nationals near Zuqar Island in the southern Red Sea, close to the Bab al-Mandab strait, and that their forces carried out a rescue operation.

Houthi military spokesperson Yahya Saree said on X that preliminary information indicated Saudi Arabia had struck a vessel transporting Indian citizens near the island. "This reckless act by the Saudi enemy threatens international navigation in the Red Sea, and the international community must stop the Saudi enemy from these reckless actions," he said, according to AzerNews.

What Is Verified, and What Is Not

The yacht claim rests, so far, on the Houthi statement alone. No Saudi response, Indian government confirmation, or independent reporting from the scene had corroborated it in the accounts published on Thursday, and the condition of the 14 Indians was not confirmed. Nation Press noted the claim "had not been independently verified at the time of reporting." Readers should treat the rescue and the circumstances of the alleged strike as unconfirmed until New Delhi or Riyadh speaks.

A Week of Indian Casualties in the Kingdom

The claim landed a day after a deadly sequence inside Saudi Arabia. On October 21, an attack on King Fahd International Airport in Dammam killed one Indian national and injured two others, the Indian Embassy confirmed. The same day, debris from an intercepted drone at Saudi Aramco's Shaybah oil field killed a Filipino and a Nepali worker and injured an Indian and a Pakistani worker, according to the Saudi Energy Ministry.

India's Ministry of External Affairs condemned the attacks. "We strongly condemn the continued attacks on civilian and energy infrastructure in Saudi Arabia, including the attack on King Fahd International Airport in Dammam and Saudi Aramco's Shaybah oil field in the Eastern Province on October 21. These attacks have unfortunately resulted in civilian deaths and injuries," the ministry said.

Why the Red Sea Claim Matters

Zuqar Island sits near the southern entrance to the Red Sea, a route Houthi attacks have disrupted since 2023, forcing shipping diversions that raise costs for Indian trade. An attack on a vessel crewed by Indian nationals, if verified, would extend the week's pattern — Indians caught in strikes on Saudi soil — to the sea lanes themselves. About 2.74 million Indian nationals live in Saudi Arabia, and the Indian Embassy has urged them to stay alert, follow local authority instructions, shelter indoors during aerial attacks, and avoid filming interceptions or impact sites.

The United States has ordered the departure of non-emergency diplomats and family members from its missions in Saudi Arabia amid the escalation. Yemen's defence ministry, meanwhile, has warned that rallies supporting the Houthis in areas under their control could be considered military targets.
